1. Unsupported fact. Under "Which hall is newer inside?" the page says "Cornell closed it for more than two years for its first full renovation in six decades." The cited news page (peek-inside-balch-hall-renovations-near-completion) says only "first significant construction project since the summer of 2000, and first overall renovation in six decades". It says nothing about a closure or a duration. "Closed ... for more than two years" is invented. Also, "First full renovation in six decades" in the "Recent work" table cell overstates "first overall renovation in six decades".

2. Overreach beyond the source. The Sun article (Nov. 2025) gives one anecdote: a sophomore transfer with a 7:30 p.m. last-day timeslot was left with Clara Dickson triples and Sheldon Court doubles. The page turns it into "It also makes it a common landing spot when selection runs late". The sophomore reader block repeats it as "Do not count on a double in Dickson if your slot is late, because triples are what remain." Neither the article nor Cornell supports a general claim about Dickson.

The page never says Balch is women-only. The table says "First-year women".
